answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments ensure that an identity is not a mere echo of a relic state, while sequential delay functions prevent agents from letting their clones wander through the state space. Information-theoretic unforgeability arises from the hardness of forging these commitments, ensuring cryptographic finality. This construction renders identity spoofing computationally infeasible via VRF sortition, enforcing Byzantine fault tolerance.
